strengths: Separated curling smoke lobes replace the rejected spheres, capsule and procedural ribbon silhouettes.
The same deterministic sparse-volume sequence remains spatially legible in warm historic and cool contemporary lighting without host-specific VFX adaptation.
Complete temporal renders show continuous buoyant rise, lateral drift and evolving density without obvious volume popping.
Embers remain source-bound and provide restrained warm depth separation through the plume.
limitations: The approximately 4.6 centimetre voxel grid is accepted for medium and background framing, not close or hero-close smoke photography.
The half-second verification fixture proves local continuity but not a long-lived plume, looping behaviour or interaction with moving collision geometry.
Embers are simplified volumetric points and are not accepted as close-range spark or firework inventory.
The project-owned solver models buoyant incompressible advection and vorticity confinement but does not yet model combustion chemistry, obstacles or adaptive-resolution turbulence.
notes: Accepted after V1-V5 analytic representations were rejected and V6 full transfer failed the unchanged contemporary framing gate. V7 preserves the gate, moves the frontal contemporary camera 0.25 metres back, passes complete two-host Cycles renders, and visibly demonstrates a reusable source-bound turbulent volume at its declared medium-shot tier.
